title: Retirement handshake and regional variant mediator for pinned model versions
creator: Marina Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement a resilient ‘retirement handshake’ and regional variant mediator that gracefully routes requests for pinned model versions when the exact pinned binary is unavailable (deprecation, regional capacity constraints, or incompatible runtime). This ticket covers policy design, runtime routing logic, API contract changes, rollout strategy, required telemetry, and automated migration playbooks.

Scope:
- A deterministic compatibility check (model signature + ABI) to decide when a non-pinned variant is acceptable.
- Regional variant mediator that evaluates fallback candidates by (1) compatibility score, (2) historical latency/quality for this customer, (3) capacity/SLAs for candidate region.
- Retirement handshake: an automated negotiation flow that attempts to warm candidate variants, run a short compatibility eval, and only then redirect production traffic according to configured risk thresholds.
- Deprecation windowing: allow pinned versions to declare a retiring_at timestamp + grace period; outbound notifications to customers and in-console guidance for 'soft pin' vs 'hard pin' behaviour.
- APIs & Console UX: new pin metadata fields (retiring_at, compatibility_whitelist, fallback_policy), and an observability panel showing fallback counts, quality regression delta, and warmup status.
- Rollout & SLOs: default risk policy: prefer same-region compatible quantized variants, then cross-region variants with <5ms median added latency, fall back to less-preferred variants only under capacity violation. Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs where possible and flag deviations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility check implemented and unit-tested in runtime (coverage >= 85%).
- Mediator decision graph implemented as a lightweight, auditable state machine with deterministic logging for every fallback event.
- Console surface displays fallback events by customer & route, including reason codes and before/after latency/quality deltas.
- Automated warmup flow that can prefetch KV caches and run a 100-sample eval against the customer’s eval set within the retirement window.
- End-to-end e2e test that simulates a regional capacity loss and demonstrates successful graceful retirement with at most one percent increased token cost and no drop in quality beyond configured thresholds.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Marina Chen: Initial scoping completed. Interviewed two cust-facing PMs; primary ask is predictable latency and a clear migration timeline for pinned customers. Added deprecation window concept to spec.

2026-02-26 - Daniel Brooks: Prototype compatibility checksum implemented (model-arch + tokenization hash). Early results: lightweight and fast, but false-positive risk on custom finetunes — added 'compatibility_whitelist' for customer-specified allowances.

2026-03-01 - SRE (Liam O'Neal): Raised concern about warmup traffic increasing cost spikes. Decided to limit warmup to bounded request budget (configurable per-customer) and use synthetic warmup when possible.

2026-03-03 - Emily Park (Product): Reviewed UX copy for deprecation notices. Request: include recommended replacement variant and estimated delta in latency/cost in the console notification. Added to console tasks.
2026-03-06 - QA (Ravi Singh): Added checklist for e2e tests: simulate cross-region failover, measure median/95/99 latency, verify compatibility eval passes before redirecting live traffic.

2026-03-10 - Daniel Brooks: Mediator state machine skeleton merged to branch; PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9482. Needs security review for audit logging format (PII risk minimal).

2026-03-12 - Security (Aisha Kapoor): Quick review completed; recommended redacting customer identifiers in debug logs and routing full identifiers only to internal audit logs (KMS-protected). Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-14 - Daniel Brooks: Implemented telemetry counters for 'fallback_reason' and 'compatibility_score'. Hooked to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/retirement-handshake. Next: iterate on fallback ranking weights using historical request traces.
